title: rollout-start
description: Starts a staged rollout of one release (docs/spec/07-upgrade-channel.md "Staged rollout"). Batch 1 is the one cabinet named here, the canary. Without a target the rollout is for the whole fleet; with one it is for a client, a site or chosen cabinets, and the canary must be one of them (plan item 2.11, decision-log D161). Without batches, batch 2 is the in-office cabinets, batch 3 about 5 percent of the rest and batch 4 everyone else; with batches, each one after the canary is a number of cabinets or a share of those left after the canary, in-office cabinets first, and whatever remains is a last batch. A batch must reach successRatePercent before the next starts; failures above failureLimitPercent of a batch pause the rollout on their own. A release is one version for one Windows architecture (docs/spec/18-built-designs.md §1), so the version alone does not name one: the architecture does, and only cabinets built for it are ever targets - the others could not run the package at all.

architecture.description: Which Windows the release being rolled out is for. Cabinets of the other architecture are left out of every batch and counted in the audit as wrongArchitecture, so a rollout can never offer a package a cabinet cannot run.

target.description: Which cabinets the rollout is for. Omitted, the whole fleet.

batches.description: The batches after the canary, in order: each a number of cabinets or a share (percent) of the cabinets left after the canary. What remains after the last is one more batch. At most eight, so a rollout has at most ten.

stepUpToken.description: A one-time step-up token bound to this exact action.
